advice: Rest, drink warm fluids, and use steam inhalation. Usually resolves in 5-7 days.
Rest, stay hydrated, and take paracetamol for fever. See a doctor if fever crosses 103°F.
Drink ORS frequently and avoid solid food for a few hours. See a doctor if it lasts more than 24 hours.
Drink water and ORS immediately, rest in a cool place. Seek help if confusion or fainting occurs.
Rest in a dark, quiet room and stay hydrated. See a doctor if headaches become frequent.
Keep the area clean and dry, avoid scratching. See a doctor if pus or spreading redness appears.
These symptoms can indicate a heart attack. Go to the nearest hospital or call emergency services immediately. Do not wait.
Rest the leg, apply a cold compress, and elevate it. See a doctor if swelling is sudden or one leg is more swollen than the other (possible clot).
Rest on a firm surface, avoid heavy lifting, apply a warm compress. See a doctor if pain spreads down the leg or you lose bladder control.
Rest the joint, use a warm compress, and avoid overexertion. See a doctor if a joint is hot, red, or you have a fever alongside.
Avoid inserting anything into the ear. Keep it dry. See a doctor for proper examination and antibiotics if needed.
Avoid touching or rubbing the eyes, wash hands often. See a doctor if vision is affected or pain is severe.
Rinse with warm salt water, avoid very hot/cold food. See a dentist as soon as possible to prevent infection spreading.
Drink plenty of water. See a doctor for antibiotics - untreated UTIs can spread to the kidneys.
May indicate low iron. Eat iron-rich food (leafy greens, jaggery). See a doctor for a blood test.
If breathing is severely difficult or lips/fingertips turn blue, this is an emergency - seek urgent medical care immediately.
If there is swelling of the face/throat or difficulty breathing, this can be life-threatening - go to a hospital immediately.
For snake bites: keep the person still, keep the bite below heart level, and get to a hospital immediately - do not cut or suck the wound.
Cool the burn under running water for 10-20 minutes. Do not apply ice, toothpaste, or oil. See a doctor for large or deep burns.
Clean the wound and apply firm pressure to stop bleeding. See a doctor if bleeding doesn't stop or the cut is deep.
These can indicate dangerously high blood pressure. Seek medical attention promptly, especially if headache is sudden and severe.
These may indicate diabetes. Get a blood sugar test done at your nearest health centre.
Fever lasting more than 3-4 days with these symptoms needs a blood test. Visit a health centre for typhoid testing.
Yellowing of skin/eyes needs medical evaluation of the liver. See a doctor for a blood test soon.
High fever with joint pain and rash needs urgent testing, especially in mosquito-prone areas. Go to a health centre promptly.
Common in rural areas. Go to the nearest health centre for a blood test as soon as possible.
Try slow, deep breathing and sit somewhere calm. If chest pain or breathlessness is severe, treat it as urgent and seek care.
Keep a regular sleep schedule, avoid caffeine late in the day. See a doctor if this continues for more than 2 weeks.
Could be due to poor sleep, diet, or an underlying condition. If it persists for over 2 weeks, get a general checkup.
